data_disclaimer: SYNTHETIC. These are invented past cases used to give the historical-case specialist something to retrieve. No real case, customer or reviewer is represented.
contamination_note: This corpus and the eval case bank were authored by the same person, so lexical overlap between a precedent summary and a case summary is not evidence that retrieval generalises. The harness report treats a strong historical_case result as suspect for exactly this reason.

precedents.summary: Burst of 30 sub-$5 digital goods authorisations in 18 minutes on a 2-day-old account, 60% declined, session on a commercial VPN.
precedents.resolution_notes: Enumeration against a stolen BIN range. Card range blocked at the issuer; account closed same day.

precedents.summary: Twelve gift card authorisations under $3 across two merchants inside half an hour, unverified KYC, device seen on four accounts.
precedents.resolution_notes: Same device fingerprint as two accounts closed the previous week. Declined.

precedents.summary: Slow probing: nine low-value digital goods attempts spread over five hours with an elevated decline rate on a 6-week-old account.
precedents.resolution_notes: Deliberately paced to stay under velocity rules. Caught on the decline clustering, not the rate.

precedents.summary: Repeated small failed authorisations on a long-tenured account with otherwise normal grocery and fuel spend and verified KYC.
precedents.resolution_notes: Card details compromised offline; testing hidden inside the genuine customer's normal traffic. Only the decline burst separated it.

precedents.summary: Four-year-old account, brand new device from a hosting ASN 12000km away, followed immediately by a high-value electronics purchase far above baseline.
precedents.resolution_notes: Customer confirmed they had not travelled. Credentials reused from an unrelated breach.

precedents.summary: Device change followed by a money transfer to a service the account had never used, transaction amount itself unremarkable.
precedents.resolution_notes: Cash-out attempt after credential stuffing. Amount was kept low deliberately to stay under review thresholds.

precedents.summary: Overnight session from an unfamiliar country then three retail charges well above the account's usual amounts.
precedents.resolution_notes: Session token replay. Chargebacks filed on all three charges.

precedents.summary: Takeover from the victim's own city on a fresh device, spending into a crypto exchange the account had never touched.
precedents.resolution_notes: Local attacker, no geographic signal at all. Category first-use plus the new device carried the decision.

precedents.summary: Three-week-old account with a failed KYC document check loading prepaid cards; device shared with five other new accounts.
precedents.resolution_notes: Fabricated identity in a cluster of six. All six closed.

precedents.summary: Account nurtured with small subscription and retail spend for six weeks, then a single large crypto exchange cash-out; unverified SSN.
precedents.resolution_notes: Classic bust-out. The nurture period is what makes these expensive: the baseline looks real by the time it matters.

precedents.summary: Identity passed KYC on fabricated documents and held eight months of tenure before a large money transfer; no shared identifiers with any other account.
precedents.resolution_notes: Only found retrospectively when the document vendor was compromised. Network analysis had nothing to offer here and correctly said so.

precedents.summary: Eight accounts converging on two device fingerprints and a single payment instrument, all forwarding to the same transfer service.
precedents.resolution_notes: Mule network. Every member had clean KYC and clean device history individually; only the graph showed it.

precedents.summary: Verified long-tenured account with spotless identity signals sitting inside a six-account ring over device and payment method.
precedents.resolution_notes: Recruited mule using their own real identity. Identity checks are useless against this pattern by construction.

precedents.summary: Three accounts sharing one payment instrument with repeat transfers, deliberately small enough to stay under ring-size heuristics.
precedents.resolution_notes: Cell size tuned to evade a ring-size threshold. Repeat-transfer pattern was the deciding evidence.

precedents.summary: Customer abroad on holiday: foreign IP, large hotel charge above their usual amounts, but the device was their own and travel was gradual.
precedents.resolution_notes: False positive from the geo rule. Prior countries on file already included this destination.

precedents.summary: Three family accounts on one residential IP range with ordinary supermarket and transport spend and no device sharing.
precedents.resolution_notes: Household, not a ring. Shared IP range alone should never carry a decline.

precedents.summary: Long-tenured customer on a commercial VPN making a large one-off electronics purchase; no ring links and enhanced KYC on file.
precedents.resolution_notes: Privacy-conscious customer. VPN use correlates with fraud weakly and with privacy preference strongly; declining on it alone costs good customers.

precedents.summary: New customer in their first week: thin transaction history and a newly seen device, modest retail purchase, clean KYC and no shared identifiers.
precedents.resolution_notes: Every new customer looks like this. Treating a thin baseline as risk is how onboarding conversion dies.

precedents.summary: Eleven small transactions in one afternoon at merchants the account uses every month, no declines, same device as always.
precedents.resolution_notes: Payday behaviour. Velocity without novelty is not a fraud signal.

precedents.summary: Business account making regular prepaid reload purchases for staff; elevated-risk merchant category used consistently for over a year.
precedents.resolution_notes: Category risk weights are population statistics, not statements about this account. Repeat use is the defence.

precedents.summary: New device from a new country on a long-lived account but with an entirely ordinary amount at an ordinary merchant.
signals: identity risk vs clean transaction profile
precedents.resolution_notes: Escalated to a human, who reached the customer. Genuine travel with a replacement phone. The signals genuinely did not resolve without contacting the customer.

precedents.summary: Four accounts sharing a single household device with clean identity and clean transaction profiles across all four.
signals: network risk vs clean identity and transactions
precedents.resolution_notes: Escalated on conflicting signals; the human found three of the four accounts had been opened within an hour of each other. That fact was not visible to any single specialist.
